# <span id="aanchor38"></span> Install & Configure Services

After installing FLOWCAL, the system administrator will need to install the applicable FLOWCAL services. Most services are related to a FLOWCAL module, an add-on, or TESTit Integrated, depending on the software purchased. Only services purchased and the functionality to be utilized should be installed.

Depending on operation size, customers may have one or more application servers, and each server has the capacity to run one or more services. Balancing services across servers and running multiple instances of the same service allows FLOWCAL to divide the work of processing data across multiple servers and services.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Installing">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Install Services</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Installing">

This FLOWCAL installation folder includes all FLOWCAL services. Most FLOWCAL services can be easily identified because the application file names begin with "FcSrv." FLOWCAL services must be installed manually and do not come pre-installed with the system.

At a minimum, the FcSrvMtrRollup.exe service and the FcSrvLcnRollup.exe service must be installed.

If the file import service is being utilized to import data files automatically, the FcSrvFileImport.exe service must be installed. If the Source Analysis module has been purchased, the GQTrans.exe service must be installed.  
  
The Oracle client must be installed and the FLOWCAL services account must be configured within the Services Login section of the Service Configuration screen before FLOWCAL services are installed and started.

<div class="procedure">

To install services:

1.  Locate the **\_installServices.bat** file in the FLOWCAL installation folder. This is a Windows batch command script that lists all the services provided by FLOWCAL.
2.  Right-click the **\_installServices.bat** file to edit it using Notepad.
3.  Each line item begins with "rem" ("remark") which tells Windows to ignore that line item. Remove the remarks indicators from the services to be installed. For example: to install the file import service, delete the "rem" indicator from the "rem FcSrvFileImport.exe /install" line.
4.  Save and close the batch command script.
5.  Double-click the **\_installServices.bat** batch command script to install the designated services.

If the install is successful, a window displays with a "Successfully Installed" indicator for each service. If the install fails, the window displays a "Failed" instead.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Multiple Copies">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Install Multiple Copies of a Service</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Multiple Copies">

Most standard services can be installed in multiples to distribute the processing of data across multiple services.

<div class="procedure">

To install a copy of a service:

1.  Create a copy of the applicable service from the FLOWCAL installation directory. For example: to run a copy of the FcSrvLcnRollup service, copy the service and name the copy FcSrvLcnRollup2.
2.  Login to FLOWCAL and set the Total FLOWCAL Installations field within the Service Configuration screen to the maximum number of any given service. For example: If there are two Meter Rollups services installed and three Location Rollups services installed, set this value to 3.
3.  By default, the \_installServices.bat script contains only one of each FLOWCAL service. Copy and paste a command line (e.g., “FcSrvLcnRollup.exe /install”) within the script and append the incremental number to service name (e.g., “FcSrvLcnRollup2.exe /install”). The numbering must match the executable name exactly.
4.  When all edits are complete, save and close the batch command script.
5.  Double-click the **\_installServices.bat** batch command script to install the designated services.

Contact <a href="mailto:flowcal.support@quorumsoftware.com" class="notelink">Customer Support</a> for a recommendation of how many services to run for the FLOWCAL installation. This will vary per customer depending on variables such as number of meters, locations, and hardware specifications.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Security">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Service Security</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Security">

The Reports and File Import services may require that the service log use a network account with elevated privileges, configured in the Microsoft Services console, if accessing other servers on the network.

<div class="procedure">

To configure the log on for the File Import service:

1.  Click the Windows Start button, type “Services” in the find field, and press **Enter**. This launches the Services console.
2.  Scroll down in the list of services until you find **FcSrvFileImport**. Right-click **FcSrvFileImport** and select **Properties**.
3.  Click the **Log On** tab.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" />

1.  Select **This Account**.
2.  Enter the account name and password, which will be used by the file import service when determining permissions to the network import folder.
3.  Click **OK**.
4.  Repeat steps 1 through 6 for the Reports service.

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Uninstall">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Uninstall Services</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Uninstall">

The FLOWCAL installation folder contains a corresponding "\_uninstallServices.bat" file that is used to uninstall the services. Stop the services and follow the service installation steps; note however that the batch command script contains commands to perform uninstalls for each designated service.

When uninstalling copies of any given service, remember to adjust the Total FLOWCAL Installations field within the Service Configuration screen accordingly. You do not have to be an administrator on the server to uninstall services.

</div>
